# mcp-gmap-rs / en

https://fcenedes.github.io/mcp-gmap-rs/


<!-- https://fcenedes.github.io/mcp-gmap-rs/guide/agent-skill -->

# Agent skill

The portable `mcp-gmap` skill teaches an agent how to choose tools, call MCP or CLI safely, inspect partial failures and retain Google attribution. It supplements the executable or MCP connection you configure separately.

## Install from source or a release

The source package and every release archive include [the skill folder](https://github.com/fcenedes/mcp-gmap-rs/tree/main/skills/mcp-gmap). From a checkout or extracted archive, install it for Codex:

```sh
mkdir -p "${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills"
cp -R skills/mcp-gmap "${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills/"
```

Invoke it as `$mcp-gmap`, for example:

> Use $mcp-gmap to find cafes near Gare de Lyon, compare walking routes and preserve source links.

For other agents, place the same folder in their supported skill directory, or load `SKILL.md` and its linked references. The instruction body is agent-independent; `agents/openai.yaml` provides optional Codex UI metadata. Install a working executable on the agent’s PATH or configure its [MCP connection](./mcp).

## What the skill adds

The skill starts with tool discovery, so it does not assume that an older installed release exposes the newest catalog. It prefers exact coordinates and returned place IDs, keeps search scopes small, and chooses dedicated tools for address validation, aggregate counts or along-route search instead of approximating those operations from unrelated results.

It treats credentials as process/deployment configuration, never tool arguments. It distinguishes inbound MCP authorization from outbound Google access and uses offline diagnostics first. Live diagnostic probes are potentially billable. Composite output must be checked for nested errors, even when the top-level call succeeds.

The [tool-selection reference](https://github.com/fcenedes/mcp-gmap-rs/blob/main/skills/mcp-gmap/references/tool-selection.md) explains the decision rules. The [CLI reference](https://github.com/fcenedes/mcp-gmap-rs/blob/main/skills/mcp-gmap/references/cli.md) covers structured invocation and access diagnostics. See this manual’s [recipes](./recipes) for complete workflows and [tool reference](../reference/tools) for every argument.


<!-- https://fcenedes.github.io/mcp-gmap-rs/guide/authentication -->

# Authentication

Configure outbound Google credentials separately from the credentials used by MCP HTTP clients. API-key mode is the default; setting a service-account path alone does not enable OAuth.

## API-key and OAuth coverage

| Endpoint family | API key | OAuth in this executable |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Places (New), Routes, Weather, Air Quality, Address Validation, Places Aggregate | Yes | Yes |
| Geocoding v3, Elevation, Time Zone, Maps Static, Pollen, Roads | Yes | No |

Named-location resolution and composite calls may require a key even when their main operation supports OAuth. Use exact coordinate inputs to avoid unnecessary geocoding. OAuth failures never silently fall back to an API key. See [Google Cloud setup](./google-cloud) to enable the exact services and restrict a key.

## Service-account OAuth


In OAuth mode, Places (New), Routes, Weather, Air Quality, Address Validation and
Places Aggregate requests receive an
OAuth **access token** and an `X-Goog-User-Project` header. This project requests
the `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform` scope documented by those
APIs. Google’s Rust auth library obtains, caches and refreshes the tokens.
`GOOGLE_MAPS_TIMEOUT` also bounds credential initialization and token acquisition.
No manually pasted access token or application OAuth consent screen is needed
for the service-account flow. See [Maps server-side OAuth guidance](https://developers.google.com/maps/api-security-best-practices#use-oauth-for-server-side-apps).

Create a dedicated service account and grant it permission to consume services
on the project used for Maps billing/quota:

```sh
export PROJECT_ID='your-project-id'
export SA_EMAIL="mcp-gmap@${PROJECT_ID}.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
gcloud iam service-accounts create mcp-gmap --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
  --display-name='MCP Google Maps'
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding "$PROJECT_ID" \
  --member="serviceAccount:${SA_EMAIL}" \
  --role='roles/serviceusage.serviceUsageConsumer'
```

The Service Usage Consumer role includes `serviceusage.services.use` for quota
and billing. It does not grant the ability to enable services or create keys;
those setup steps need a separately authorized administrator. Enable the Maps
APIs in the quota project using the [Google Cloud setup guide](./google-cloud). See [Service Usage permissions](https://docs.cloud.google.com/service-usage/docs/access-control).

Choose one credential source below. The same settings work with CLI, stdio and
HTTP. Configuration follows the usual file → environment → flag precedence.

### A. Mounted service-account JSON key

If your organization permits JSON keys, open **IAM & Admin → Service Accounts**,
select the account, then **Keys → Add key → Create new key → JSON**. Save it
outside the source checkout. Alternatively:

```sh
mkdir -p "$HOME/.config/mcp-gmap-rs"
gcloud iam service-accounts keys create \
  "$HOME/.config/mcp-gmap-rs/service-account.json" \
  --iam-account="$SA_EMAIL" --project="$PROJECT_ID"
chmod 600 "$HOME/.config/mcp-gmap-rs/service-account.json"
export GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS="$HOME/.config/mcp-gmap-rs/service-account.json"
export GOOGLE_CLOUD_QUOTA_PROJECT="$PROJECT_ID"
export GOOGLE_MAPS_AUTH_MODE=oauth
```

For a mounted file, the equivalent `.env` is:

```dotenv
GOOGLE_MAPS_AUTH_MODE=oauth
GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS=/credentials/service-account.json
GOOGLE_CLOUD_QUOTA_PROJECT=your-project-id
# Optional, for Geocoding v3 / Elevation / Time Zone / Static Maps / Pollen / Roads:
# GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY=your-restricted-api-key
```

Set the credential path only when using a readable JSON file; do not set it to
an empty string or to the JSON contents.
Relative paths are resolved from the working directory. File values are used
directly, without mutating the process environment. The loader also accepts ADC
`external_account`, `impersonated_service_account` and `authorized_user` JSON
configurations. Restart the process after changing a credential file.

Service-account keys are long-lived credentials. Prefer the keyless options
below when available; keep JSON keys out of Git and image layers, and rotate or
delete unused keys. Google documents [key creation and organization policies](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/keys-create-delete).

### B. Application Default Credentials without a JSON key

Leave `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` unset in both the process environment and
the selected dotenv file or Kubernetes Secret/ConfigMap. Shell `unset` alone does
not remove a file-layer value; remove the entry rather than setting an empty path.
Then set:

```dotenv
GOOGLE_MAPS_AUTH_MODE=oauth
GOOGLE_CLOUD_QUOTA_PROJECT=your-project-id
```

The official auth library uses [Application Default Credentials (ADC)](https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/authentication/application-default-credentials):
local ADC credentials when present, otherwise the attached workload/service
account through the metadata server. Credential discovery is lazy: `tools`,
`schema` and help work without fetching a token. An OAuth API call needs a quota
project and valid credentials.

For local development with service-account impersonation, enable the IAM
Credentials API and grant your developer account Token Creator on the service
account, then create local ADC credentials:

```sh
gcloud services enable iamcredentials.googleapis.com --project="$PROJECT_ID"
gcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding "$SA_EMAIL" \
  --project="$PROJECT_ID" --member='user:you@example.com' \
  --role='roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator'
unset GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
gcloud auth application-default login --impersonate-service-account="$SA_EMAIL"
export GOOGLE_MAPS_AUTH_MODE=oauth
export GOOGLE_CLOUD_QUOTA_PROJECT="$PROJECT_ID"
```

This uses a short-lived service-account token for Maps calls without downloading
its private key. See [service-account impersonation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/service-account-impersonation).

### C. Kubernetes and GKE workload identity

For generic Kubernetes, mount the credential JSON as a Secret file and set the
three OAuth variables in option A. The file must be readable by UID 10001 used
by the container. Mount it read-only and keep `MCP_HTTP_TOKEN` in its own runtime
Secret. [The container guide](./deployment) explains the base Deployment.

On GKE, prefer [Workload Identity Federation for GKE](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/workload-identity)
with a Kubernetes ServiceAccount linked to the IAM service account. Enable it
for your cluster/node pool first (Autopilot already enables it), then:

```sh
gcloud services enable iamcredentials.googleapis.com --project="$PROJECT_ID"
kubectl create serviceaccount mcp-gmap-rs --namespace default
gcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding "$SA_EMAIL" \
  --project="$PROJECT_ID" --role='roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser' \
  --member="serviceAccount:${PROJECT_ID}.svc.id.goog[default/mcp-gmap-rs]"
kubectl annotate serviceaccount mcp-gmap-rs --namespace default \
  "iam.gke.io/gcp-service-account=${SA_EMAIL}"
kubectl patch deployment mcp-gmap-rs --namespace default --type=merge \
  -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"serviceAccountName":"mcp-gmap-rs"}}}}'
kubectl set env deployment/mcp-gmap-rs --namespace default \
  GOOGLE_MAPS_AUTH_MODE=oauth GOOGLE_CLOUD_QUOTA_PROJECT="$PROJECT_ID"
```

These commands assume the cluster and IAM service account are in `PROJECT_ID`
and the base Deployment is in `default`. Adjust project/namespace names for
your installation. Do not set `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` for this metadata
flow. The pod obtains access tokens through the GKE metadata server. Outside
GKE, an `external_account` credential configuration plus the provider's projected
identity token can be used with Google's Workload Identity Federation setup.

For OAuth-only operation, remove the Google API key from the runtime Secret and
enable only tools/inputs whose calls stay on OAuth-supported APIs. Keep the key
when using the key-only endpoints from the table or composite flows that need
them. OAuth failures on supported APIs fail explicitly; they never silently
downgrade to the key.

## Verify and troubleshoot

```sh
mcp-gmap-rs --auth-mode oauth search-places --query 'coffee in Paris'
mcp-gmap-rs --auth-mode oauth weather --latitude 48.8584 --longitude 2.2945
```

These are real, potentially billable calls. Check the effective mode and quota
project when testing; OAuth billing uses `GOOGLE_CLOUD_QUOTA_PROJECT`, while
key-authenticated calls use the key's project. The projects may differ.

Use `mcp-gmap-rs doctor` for offline configuration checks, or `doctor --live` for
explicitly billable API probes. The [production guide](./production) describes
the report and tool filtering.

With OAuth variables exported, run the six opt-in live acceptance tests with:

```sh
cargo test --locked --test live live_oauth_ -- --ignored --test-threads=1
```

These tests explicitly remove the API key from each child process, so a passing
test exercises OAuth. They cover Places, Routes, Weather, Air Quality, Address
Validation and Places Aggregate and
require their APIs enabled. They do not load `.env`; export the OAuth settings
or run in a configured workload. Ordinary tests/CI use local token/API fixtures
and do not require a service account or contact Google.

| Symptom | Check |
| --- | --- |
| `GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY is required` | The selected operation reaches a key-only endpoint, or API-key mode is selected. |
| OAuth authentication failed | Credential path/type, key validity, workload identity/impersonation binding, IAM Credentials API when used, token-endpoint connectivity and clock accuracy. Application errors omit credential contents and tokens. |
| `GOOGLE_CLOUD_QUOTA_PROJECT is required` | Set the Maps consumer project ID/number for OAuth calls. |
| Google `403` / API disabled | Enable the exact service in the consumer project; ensure billing and Service Usage permission. |
| API-key IP denial | Match restrictions to the server or cluster's public egress IP. |
| Token timeout | Allow access to Google token/STS/IAM endpoints or the workload metadata server; review `GOOGLE_MAPS_TIMEOUT`. |
| HTTP `401` from this MCP server | Send its `MCP_HTTP_TOKEN`; Google service-account tokens authenticate a separate outbound connection. |


<!-- https://fcenedes.github.io/mcp-gmap-rs/guide/cli -->

# Command-line interface

Use the CLI for one-shot queries, shell automation and structured subprocess calls. Every tool shares its input schema and implementation with MCP.

## Discover the installed interface

```sh
mcp-gmap-rs --version
mcp-gmap-rs --help
mcp-gmap-rs tools
mcp-gmap-rs schema search-nearby
mcp-gmap-rs search-nearby --help
```

`tools` reports the enabled tools and their schemas. Check your installed version rather than assuming that every capability in the newest manual is present. Running without a subcommand starts the stdio server, so always supply a command for one-shot automation.

## Flags or shared JSON

Tool commands use kebab-case flags; object and array values take JSON. Boolean flags accept `true` or `false`, and a bare boolean flag means `true`.

```sh
mcp-gmap-rs search-nearby \
  --center '{"value":"48.8584,2.2945","isCoordinates":true}' \
  --keyword cafe --radius 500 --open-now
```

The generic `call` interface accepts either a logical MCP tool name or CLI command name and uses the exact MCP argument object:

```sh
mcp-gmap-rs call maps_geocode --args '{"address":"Paris, France"}'
printf '%s' '{"address":"Paris, France"}' | mcp-gmap-rs call geocode --args -
```

When launching a subprocess programmatically, pass serialized JSON as a distinct argument. Avoid interpolating untrusted text into shell command strings. Top-level parameters have flags; nested fields stay inside JSON objects.

## Output and failure handling

Ordinary tool results are JSON on stdout. Errors go to stderr and produce a nonzero exit status. `doctor` also writes its JSON report to stdout when checks fail. Batch, matrix and composite results can contain per-item errors even when the command exits successfully: inspect those fields before treating the whole operation as complete.

```sh
mcp-gmap-rs place-details --place-id ChIJLU7jZClu5kcR4PcOOO6p3I0 --output place.json
mcp-gmap-rs static-map --center Paris --zoom 12 --output paris.png
```

`--output` writes JSON for ordinary tools and raw PNG for a static map. Without it, CLI static-map output contains base64 data. Times generally use RFC 3339 with an explicit timezone; the Time Zone tool’s optional `timestamp` is Unix **milliseconds**. See [all tools and examples](../reference/tools).


<!-- https://fcenedes.github.io/mcp-gmap-rs/guide/configuration -->

# Configuration

The CLI and both MCP transports share the same startup configuration. Choose a file for local work, environment injection for containers, and flags for explicit per-process overrides.

## Precedence

Values are applied in this order, with later layers taking priority:

**Built-in defaults → optional dotenv file → process environment → CLI flags**

The default file is `.env` in the current working directory. Parent directories are not searched. A missing default file is allowed; an unreadable or malformed file fails startup without printing its contents.

```sh
mcp-gmap-rs --env-file /etc/mcp-gmap/runtime.env serve http
mcp-gmap-rs --no-env-file tools
```

`MCP_ENV_FILE` selects a file too, while `--env-file` takes precedence. An explicitly selected file must exist. `--no-env-file` disables file loading, including `MCP_ENV_FILE`; it conflicts with `--env-file`. Dotenv parsing does not mutate the process environment.

## Override a mounted configuration

```dotenv
GOOGLE_MAPS_LANGUAGE=en
GOOGLE_MAPS_TIMEOUT=30
GOOGLE_MAPS_ENABLED_TOOLS=maps_search_places,maps_place_details
```

With that file mounted, an environment variable changes the language and a flag changes the timeout:

```sh
GOOGLE_MAPS_LANGUAGE=fr mcp-gmap-rs \
  --env-file /etc/mcp-gmap/runtime.env --timeout 15 tools
```

Repeated `--allowed-host` and `--allowed-origin` flags replace their corresponding file/environment lists as a whole. An explicitly empty environment value also overrides the file: it can clear an optional token or list, while an empty timeout is invalid.

## Control the tool surface

`GOOGLE_MAPS_ENABLED_TOOLS` or `--enabled-tools` accepts comma-separated logical names such as `maps_weather,maps_air_quality`, or `*` for all tools. Unknown names fail startup. Disabled tools disappear from discovery and cannot be called. Discovery and schema inspection need no credentials, but a requested API operation must have the appropriate Google credential.

Application settings are read at startup. Restart after changing environment values, credential JSON or Kubernetes Secret/ConfigMap configuration. Native TLS certificate, key and client-CA files are the exception: they support [SIGHUP reload](./production#native-tls-and-mutual-tls).

See the [complete configuration reference](../reference/configuration) for all 21 settings, defaults, flags and ranges. Website language selection does not change `GOOGLE_MAPS_LANGUAGE`, which controls Google response text.


<!-- https://fcenedes.github.io/mcp-gmap-rs/guide/deployment -->

# Deployment

For Google API-key creation, API enablement and service-account OAuth, follow the
[Google Cloud setup guide](./google-cloud). The same layered settings work
in containers. OAuth can use a mounted JSON credential file or the workload's ADC
identity; credentials are supplied at runtime.

Download or clone the [source repository](https://github.com/fcenedes/mcp-gmap-rs), then build from its root:

```sh
docker build -t mcp-gmap-rs:local .
```

The multi-stage Dockerfile compiles with Rust 1.94.1 and the lockfile. The runtime
contains the executable, Debian CA certificates and licenses, runs as UID/GID
10001, and supports a read-only root filesystem. The allowlisted build context
excludes local `.env` files, Git data and build output. No credentials are needed
to build. BuildKit caches Cargo downloads and build output for subsequent builds.

The same Dockerfile builds natively on Linux amd64 and arm64. To build both and
push to your registry with a configured Buildx builder:

```sh
docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 \
  -t registry.example.com/your-team/mcp-gmap-rs:YOUR_VERSION --push .
```

No container registry publication is configured automatically. Replace image
names and versions with the image you built or published.

## Run HTTP, CLI or stdio

The image defaults to `serve http` on `0.0.0.0:3000`. Supply a bearer token at
runtime, for example through the same `.env` format shown in `.env.example`:

```sh
docker run --rm --read-only --cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges \
  --env-file .env -p 127.0.0.1:3000:3000 mcp-gmap-rs:local
```

Ensure `.env` contains `MCP_HTTP_TOKEN`, required because the container listens
outside loopback. Google calls use `GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY` or the OAuth settings
and credential mounts from the setup guide, depending on the enabled tools.
Clients use `http://127.0.0.1:3000/mcp` and `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
`GET /health` needs no token and does not contact Google.

Docker's `--env-file` injects environment variables. To exercise the application's
file loader instead, mount a readable file and select it:

```sh
docker run --rm --read-only \
  --mount type=bind,src="$(pwd)/.env",dst=/etc/mcp-gmap/runtime.env,readonly \
  -e GOOGLE_MAPS_LANGUAGE=fr -p 127.0.0.1:3000:3000 \
  mcp-gmap-rs:local --env-file /etc/mcp-gmap/runtime.env serve http
```

The environment overrides values in the mounted file, and CLI flags override
both. The image's `MCP_HTTP_LISTEN=0.0.0.0:3000` is also an environment value;
change it with `-e MCP_HTTP_LISTEN=...` or `--listen` if needed. To use environment
variables exclusively, pass `--no-env-file serve http`.

Override the image command for CLI or stdio use:

```sh
docker run --rm mcp-gmap-rs:local tools
docker run --rm --env-file .env mcp-gmap-rs:local geocode --address Paris
docker run --rm -i --env-file .env mcp-gmap-rs:local serve stdio
```

Use `-i` for stdio, without allocating a TTY. When writing CLI output files, mount
a directory writable by UID 10001 and use `--output` within it.

## Kubernetes

The [base Kubernetes manifest](https://github.com/fcenedes/mcp-gmap-rs/blob/main/deploy/kubernetes.yaml) supplies non-secret settings through a
ConfigMap and credentials through an existing Secret named `mcp-gmap-rs`.
Create that Secret from a local file containing `GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY` and
`MCP_HTTP_TOKEN` (the file is not committed):

```sh
kubectl create secret generic mcp-gmap-rs --from-env-file=/secure/credentials.env
```

Replace `mcp-gmap-rs:local` in the Deployment with your registry image, or load
your local image into your development cluster. Then apply the example:

```sh
kubectl apply -f deploy/kubernetes.yaml
kubectl rollout status deployment/mcp-gmap-rs
kubectl port-forward service/mcp-gmap-rs 3000:3000
```

The example targets the `default` namespace. Adjust the configured service DNS
hostnames when using another namespace or an ingress. The ClusterIP Service is
private to the cluster; use a TLS ingress/proxy for remote clients, forwarding a
Host listed in `MCP_HTTP_ALLOWED_HOSTS`, authorization, and MCP/SSE headers. Add
explicit browser origins, including ports, when required.

The deployment uses `--no-env-file` because all configuration is injected through
`envFrom`. As an alternative, mount a Secret containing a dotenv file, remove
that flag and set `args: ["--env-file", "/etc/mcp-gmap/runtime.env", "serve", "http"]`.
The projected file must be readable by UID 10001; environment variables from
Secrets or ConfigMaps still override it. See the upstream Kubernetes guidance on
[environment injection](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/inject-data-application/define-environment-variable-container/)
and [Secret volumes](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/secret/).

Application configuration is read at startup. Restart pods after changing those
Secret/ConfigMap values; native TLS files also support SIGHUP reload.
Probes use `/health` for HTTP availability; a healthy pod does not prove that a
Google API is enabled or its credentials are authorized. Google calls require
outbound HTTPS and working DNS. API-key restrictions must permit the cluster's
public egress address; OAuth requires access to its token/identity endpoints.

Keep one replica for the default in-memory MCP session store. Multiple replicas
need session affinity so each session reaches its owning pod; rolling restarts
discard sessions and clients must reconnect. Resource requests/limits in the
example are starting values to tune for your workload.

SIGTERM triggers graceful MCP/HTTP shutdown; Kubernetes allows 30 seconds in the
example. The image also runs with dropped capabilities and no privilege escalation.

## Production HTTPS, metrics and limits

The [production guide](./production) covers native TLS/mTLS, certificate reload,
the optional `deploy/gateway.yaml` HTTPS Gateway, metrics, request budgets, HTTP
rate limits, JSON logs and offline/live `doctor` checks. Pass the same TLS flags
after the image name, or inject `MCP_TLS_CERT`, `MCP_TLS_KEY` and optional
`MCP_TLS_CLIENT_CA` with read-only PEM mounts. Keep all real keys outside the image.
The default ConfigMap sets request limits and JSON logging; metrics remain off
until explicitly enabled. Its default plaintext Service is intended for the
private gateway-to-pod hop.

## OAuth credentials in a container

For a service-account JSON file, mount it read-only and set the path inside the
container, not the host path:

```sh
docker run --rm --read-only --env-file /secure/oauth.env \
  --mount type=bind,src=/secure/service-account.json,dst=/credentials/service-account.json,readonly \
  -p 127.0.0.1:3000:3000 mcp-gmap-rs:local
```

The OAuth environment file sets `GOOGLE_MAPS_AUTH_MODE=oauth`,
`GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS=/credentials/service-account.json`,
`GOOGLE_CLOUD_QUOTA_PROJECT=your-project-id` and `MCP_HTTP_TOKEN`. UID 10001 must
be able to read the mounted file. Retain an API key only for tools that require
key-only endpoints. On GKE, use the [workload identity instructions](./authentication#c-kubernetes-and-gke-workload-identity)
instead of mounting a long-lived key.


<!-- https://fcenedes.github.io/mcp-gmap-rs/guide/development -->

# Development and releases

The runtime is a standalone Rust project. CLI, MCP stdio and Streamable HTTP share the same tool implementations. The documentation website is separate authoring/build tooling; end users need only the compiled executable.

## Build and check

Clone [the repository](https://github.com/fcenedes/mcp-gmap-rs), then use its lockfile:

```sh
cargo fmt --check
cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
cargo test --all-targets --all-features --locked
cargo test --doc --all-features --locked
cargo build --release --locked
```

Rust 1.88 is the declared minimum; release binaries use Rust 1.94.1. Default tests use local Google/token fixtures and require no credentials or network access to Google. CI also checks Linux/macOS, minimum Rust, stable/nightly rustdoc, source packaging, Docker/MCP/TLS smoke scenarios and Kubernetes manifests.

After local verification, `cargo clean` reclaims generated build output; subsequent builds recompile it.

## Keep the reference complete

The canonical tool guide combines actual executable schemas with reviewed defaults, results and behavioral notes:

```sh
python3 .github/scripts/tool-reference.py --binary /path/to/mcp-gmap-rs
python3 .github/scripts/tool-reference.py --binary /path/to/mcp-gmap-rs --check --verify-examples
```

The checker strips credentials, disables dotenv loading and validates all examples at the missing-key boundary without contacting Google. Update the reviewed JSON notes when parameters or behavior change.

Live tests are opt-in and potentially billable. With an explicitly configured test key, run `cargo test --locked --test live live_maps_ -- --ignored --test-threads=1`. The six OAuth tests use the `live_oauth_` filter and remove the key from child processes. Never commit credentials or enable live tests in ordinary CI.

## Publish a version

Update the Cargo version, lockfile, changelog, install examples and release notes together. Push and wait for CI, then create an annotated matching `vX.Y.Z` tag. The Release workflow checks the exact tag, builds three native targets, verifies archives/checksums and publishes the staged draft.

The separate **Publish crate** workflow requires that published GitHub release. Dispatch it for the same tag. Store its scoped `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` in the `crates-io` GitHub environment, never in this repository. docs.rs builds automatically after crates.io publication; a GitHub release alone does not update hosted Rust documentation. Verify the actual hosted build after uploading.

See the [release procedures](https://github.com/fcenedes/mcp-gmap-rs/blob/main/docs/releases.md), [validation record](https://github.com/fcenedes/mcp-gmap-rs/blob/main/docs/validation.md) and [public Rust entry point](https://docs.rs/mcp-gmap-rs/latest/mcp_gmap_rs/fn.run.html).


<!-- https://fcenedes.github.io/mcp-gmap-rs/guide/getting-started -->

# Getting started

Install one executable, configure Google access, then use the same 23 tools from your terminal or an MCP client. This manual describes v0.3.1.

## Install

Prebuilt Linux x86_64, macOS Apple Silicon and macOS Intel binaries are available in [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/fcenedes/mcp-gmap-rs/releases). Download the archive for your machine, verify it against `SHA256SUMS`, extract it and put `mcp-gmap-rs` on your `PATH`. Linux binaries target glibc 2.35 or newer. macOS binaries are not signed or notarized.

With Rust 1.88 or newer, install from crates.io:

```sh
cargo install mcp-gmap-rs --version 0.3.1 --locked
mcp-gmap-rs --version
```

No Rust, Python or JavaScript runtime is needed after the executable is built. The host needs CA certificates, DNS and outbound HTTPS access to Google.

## Configure access

[Create a restricted key and enable services](./google-cloud), or configure [service-account OAuth](./authentication). Store credentials in an ignored `.env` in your working directory:

```dotenv
GOOGLE_MAPS_AUTH_MODE=api-key
GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY=your-restricted-api-key
```

Environment variables override the file. Keep credentials outside source control and image layers. The working directory matters: parent directories are not searched for `.env`.

## Discover, check, call

Discovery and offline diagnostics do not make Google requests:

```sh
mcp-gmap-rs tools
mcp-gmap-rs schema search-places
mcp-gmap-rs doctor
```

Then make your first potentially billable call:

```sh
mcp-gmap-rs search-places --query 'coffee near Gare de Lyon, Paris'
```

The result is JSON. Keep the returned place IDs for follow-up details rather than resolving the same names repeatedly. Read [CLI usage](./cli) for automation or [MCP integration](./mcp) to connect an agent. [Recipes](./recipes) show how to combine tools; the [complete reference](../reference/tools) documents every parameter, default and result.


<!-- https://fcenedes.github.io/mcp-gmap-rs/guide/google-cloud -->

# Google Cloud setup

This executable authenticates **outbound calls to Google** with an API key or
OAuth 2.0 credentials. `MCP_HTTP_TOKEN` independently authenticates clients
connecting to your MCP HTTP server; choosing Google OAuth does not replace it.

## Enable services and billing

In the [Google Cloud console](https://console.cloud.google.com/), select or create
a project, then link an active billing account under **Billing**. Enable the
APIs you need under **APIs & Services → Library**. Enabling an API and allowing it
in an API key's restrictions are separate steps. Calls can incur charges.

The following table describes the endpoints used by this version of the project:

| Google API | Service to enable | Authentication used here |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Places API (New)](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/places/web-service/get-api-key) | `places.googleapis.com` | API key or OAuth |
| [Routes API](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/routes/get-api-key) | `routes.googleapis.com` | API key or OAuth |
| [Weather API](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/weather/get-api-key) | `weather.googleapis.com` | API key or OAuth |
| [Air Quality API](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/air-quality/get-api-key) | `airquality.googleapis.com` | API key or OAuth |
| [Address Validation API](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/address-validation/get-api-key) | `addressvalidation.googleapis.com` | API key or OAuth |
| [Places Aggregate API](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/places-aggregate/get-api-key) | `areainsights.googleapis.com` | API key or OAuth |
| [Pollen API](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/pollen/get-api-key) | `pollen.googleapis.com` | API key |
| [Roads API](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/roads/get-api-key) | `roads.googleapis.com` | API key |
| [Geocoding API v3](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/geocoding/guides-v3/get-api-key) | `geocoding-backend.googleapis.com` | API key |
| [Elevation API](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/elevation/get-api-key) | `elevation-backend.googleapis.com` | API key |
| [Time Zone API](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/timezone/get-api-key) | `timezone-backend.googleapis.com` | API key |
| [Maps Static API](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/maps-static/get-api-key) | `static-maps-backend.googleapis.com` | API key |

To enable all twelve with an administrator's `gcloud` login:

```sh
export PROJECT_ID='your-project-id'
gcloud services enable --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
  places.googleapis.com routes.googleapis.com \
  weather.googleapis.com airquality.googleapis.com \
  geocoding-backend.googleapis.com elevation-backend.googleapis.com \
  timezone-backend.googleapis.com static-maps-backend.googleapis.com \
  addressvalidation.googleapis.com areainsights.googleapis.com \
  pollen.googleapis.com roads.googleapis.com
```

The CLI's `directions` and `distance-matrix` tools use **Routes API**, so the
legacy Directions and Distance Matrix APIs are not required. Geocoding still
uses v3 in this project; [OAuth support in Google's Geocoding v4](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/geocoding/geocoding-v4-overview) does not change
the authentication of these v3 calls. Composite tools can call multiple APIs.
Named-location resolution or fallback can require Geocoding even when the main
operation uses Places or Routes. Use coordinates when you need to avoid that
dependency, or retain a restricted key for the key-only endpoints.

## Create a restricted API key

1. Open [Google Maps Platform → Keys & Credentials](https://console.cloud.google.com/google/maps-apis/credentials)
   in the selected project and choose **Create credentials → API key**.
2. Select only the APIs from the table that this instance will use. For an
   existing key, edit its API restrictions and save them.
3. Set the application restriction to **IP addresses** for this server-side
   application. Allow the public egress IP addresses Google will see. Kubernetes
   pod/private IPs are normally not the public source address; a fixed Cloud NAT
   or other egress address makes this restriction predictable.
4. Store the key in an ignored `.env`, environment injection or a Kubernetes
   Secret. See [Google's key restriction guidance](https://developers.google.com/maps/api-security-best-practices#restrict-your-api-keys).

Example `.env`:

```dotenv
GOOGLE_MAPS_AUTH_MODE=api-key
GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY=your-restricted-api-key
```

`api-key` is the default. Supplying a service-account path alone does not change
authentication mode. Discovery does not contact Google; use a real call to
verify project billing, API enablement and restrictions:

```sh
mcp-gmap-rs geocode --address 'Paris, France'
```


## Next steps

For service-account JSON, ADC, local impersonation and GKE identity, follow
[Authentication](./authentication). Then choose [CLI](./cli) or [MCP](./mcp).
The [tool reference](../reference/tools) identifies each tool’s credential requirements.


<!-- https://fcenedes.github.io/mcp-gmap-rs/guide/mcp -->

# MCP integration

Connect an MCP host through stdio for a local child process or Streamable HTTP for a long-running service. Both expose the same enabled tool catalog and schemas.

## Local stdio

A generic MCP client configuration is:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "google-maps": {
      "command": "/absolute/path/to/mcp-gmap-rs",
      "args": ["--env-file", "/secure/mcp-gmap/runtime.env", "serve", "stdio"]
    }
  }
}
```

Use the host’s configuration format and an absolute executable path. The selected dotenv file must exist. You may inject environment variables using the host instead. This is a standalone MCP server configuration; no assistant-specific runtime plugin is required.

```sh
mcp-gmap-rs serve stdio
```

Standard input and output carry newline-delimited MCP JSON-RPC only. Diagnostics go to stderr. Running the executable without arguments starts the same transport. A container-based stdio host must attach stdin without allocating a TTY.

## Streamable HTTP

```sh
mcp-gmap-rs serve http --listen 127.0.0.1:3000
```

Set your MCP client’s Streamable HTTP URL to **`http://127.0.0.1:3000/mcp`**. Where the host supports remote MCP entries, configure the endpoint and authorization header:

```json
{
  "url": "https://maps.example.com/mcp",
  "headers": {
    "Authorization": "Bearer your-mcp-http-token"
  }
}
```

The exact wrapper around this entry depends on the MCP host. The server supports protocol negotiation and the appropriate POST, GET/SSE and DELETE session operations through the Rust MCP SDK. Use an MCP client rather than treating one isolated JSON-RPC POST as a complete session.

## Bind addresses and access

Non-loopback listeners require `MCP_HTTP_TOKEN`. Clients send that token as a bearer credential; it is separate from Google OAuth or API keys. Add the endpoint’s Host value and any actual browser origins explicitly:

```sh
mcp-gmap-rs serve http --listen 0.0.0.0:3000 \
  --allowed-host maps.example.com \
  --allowed-origin https://app.example.com:443
```

The default rejects present Origin headers unless allowlisted. Request bodies are limited to 1 MiB. `/health` checks process liveness without calling Google. For public access, configure [native TLS/mTLS or a gateway](./production). Proxies must preserve authorization and MCP protocol/session headers and allow unbuffered streaming. Sessions and Google identity are process-local; see [deployment](./deployment) before adding replicas.


<!-- https://fcenedes.github.io/mcp-gmap-rs/guide/production -->

# Production operations

This guide covers v0.3.x. All Google tools share
the same implementation across CLI, MCP stdio and Streamable HTTP.

## Native TLS and mutual TLS

The HTTP listener can serve HTTPS directly using rustls and TLS 1.2/1.3:

```sh
mcp-gmap-rs serve http --listen 0.0.0.0:3443 \
  --tls-cert /etc/mcp-gmap/tls/tls.crt \
  --tls-key /etc/mcp-gmap/tls/tls.key \
  --allowed-host maps.example.com:3443
```

Supply `MCP_HTTP_TOKEN` separately through the environment or a Secret. Clients
connect to `https://maps.example.com:3443/mcp`, verify the server certificate,
and send `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Certificate files contain a PEM leaf
certificate followed by its intermediate chain; the private key must match.
The executable does not issue certificates or implement ACME. Use your PKI,
cert-manager, or a TLS gateway for issuance and renewal.

Add `--tls-client-ca /etc/mcp-gmap/tls/client-ca.pem` to require a client
certificate signed by that CA. Native mTLS applies to every path, including
`/health` and `/metrics`, and does not replace the HTTP bearer token. Any valid
client identity under the configured trust roots is accepted at the TLS layer;
there are no per-certificate tool permissions or revocation-list checks.

On Linux/macOS, replace the files atomically, then send `SIGHUP` to reload the
certificate, key and optional client CA together. Existing connections keep their
TLS state; new handshakes use the replacement. If loading fails, the previous
configuration stays active and an error is logged without printing key material.
Mounted Kubernetes Secret files can be reloaded this way after their projection
updates. Other settings still require a process restart.

For UID/GID 10001 in the container, mount keys read-only with permissions that
allow that identity to read them; use a suitable group and `fsGroup` for projected
Secrets. With native TLS, Kubernetes HTTP probes must use `scheme: HTTPS`.
Kubelet HTTP probes cannot provide an mTLS client certificate; use a TCP probe
for that deployment, understanding that it checks the listener, not TLS or Google.

## Kubernetes TLS gateway

[the Gateway manifest](https://github.com/fcenedes/mcp-gmap-rs/blob/main/deploy/gateway.yaml) provides an HTTPS Gateway and HTTPRoute for the base
Deployment in [the base Kubernetes manifest](https://github.com/fcenedes/mcp-gmap-rs/blob/main/deploy/kubernetes.yaml). Install the Gateway API CRDs and a
conformant controller first. Replace `your-gateway-class` and `maps.example.com`,
and provision a `kubernetes.io/tls` Secret named `mcp-gmap-tls` in the same namespace.
The example uses stable Gateway/HTTPRoute v1 fields and HTTPRoute timeouts
supported since Gateway API v1.2. Check your controller's timeout support.

```sh
kubectl create secret tls mcp-gmap-tls --cert=/secure/fullchain.pem --key=/secure/key.pem
kubectl set env deployment/mcp-gmap-rs \
  MCP_HTTP_ALLOWED_HOSTS='maps.example.com,mcp-gmap-rs:3000,localhost:3000,127.0.0.1:3000'
kubectl apply -f deploy/gateway.yaml
kubectl get gateway,httproute
```

Persist the corresponding allowed-host setting in the ConfigMap or deployment
source too. Add actual browser origins with `MCP_HTTP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` when needed.
The route exposes only `/mcp`; health and metrics stay on the private Service.
Authorization and MCP session/protocol headers must pass through unchanged.
Disable response buffering/caching and configure streaming/idle timeouts in the
chosen controller. The route disables request/backend-request deadlines; configure
appropriate connection/idle limits at the gateway for your clients.

This configuration terminates TLS at the gateway and uses HTTP to the ClusterIP
backend. Use native TLS plus a controller-supported BackendTLSPolicy or a mesh if
the gateway-to-pod connection must also be encrypted. Restrict direct pod/Service
access with your cluster's network policy. TLS does not provide MCP OAuth login:
the executable uses a shared bearer token and one Google identity per process.

See the upstream [Gateway TLS guide](https://gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io/guides/user-guides/tls/)
and [HTTPRoute timeout guide](https://gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io/guides/http-timeouts/).

## Limits, retries and deadlines

| Variable | Default | Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `GOOGLE_MAPS_MAX_REQUESTS` | `200` | `--max-requests` | Google HTTP attempts per tool invocation, 1–10000; includes retries |
| `GOOGLE_MAPS_MAX_RETRIES` | `2` | `--max-retries` | Additional attempts per Google request, 0–5 |
| `GOOGLE_MAPS_TOOL_TIMEOUT` | `120` | `--tool-timeout` | Overall tool deadline in seconds, 1–3600 |
| `MCP_HTTP_RATE_LIMIT` | `120` | HTTP `--rate-limit` | Authenticated `/mcp` HTTP requests per minute per process; 0 disables |
| `MCP_METRICS_ENABLED` | `false` | HTTP `--metrics [true\|false]` | Enable protected Prometheus `/metrics` |
| `MCP_LOG_FORMAT` | `text` | `--log-format text\|json` | Diagnostic event format on stderr |
| `MCP_TLS_CERT` | unset | HTTP `--tls-cert` | PEM server certificate chain file |
| `MCP_TLS_KEY` | unset | HTTP `--tls-key` | Matching PEM server private key file |
| `MCP_TLS_CLIENT_CA` | unset | HTTP `--tls-client-ca` | PEM CA bundle; require client certificates |

These settings follow defaults → optional dotenv → environment → flags. TLS
certificate and key must be supplied together. Empty environment TLS paths clear
their file values. `GOOGLE_MAPS_TIMEOUT` bounds each Google HTTP request including
semaphore queueing, retries, backoff and response reading; OAuth acquisition has
its own bound using the same timeout. The overall tool deadline includes both.

Each invocation has a fresh request budget shared across all its concurrent
branches. Five Google API requests can execute concurrently per process. Once
the budget is exhausted, further attempts fail locally. Composites may return
successful output containing per-item budget/errors; inspect those fields. This
limits request count, not currency: different Google requests/fields have different
prices, and a matrix request can bill multiple elements.

Read-only Google requests retry HTTP 429, 500, 502, 503 and 504 and network failures.
Retries honor `Retry-After` seconds or HTTP dates, otherwise use exponential
backoff with jitter. They stay within the request deadline and invocation budget.
Other HTTP errors, including 400/401/403, are not retried. No authentication
failure silently switches to API-key mode. Set retries to zero to make a single
attempt. Google-internal legacy JSON error statuses are reported without retries.

The HTTP limiter is a token bucket with a burst capacity equal to its per-minute
rate and continuous refill. It covers initialization, POST, GET and DELETE on
`/mcp`, across all sessions. Unauthorized requests do not consume the bucket.
Rejections return HTTP 429 with `Retry-After`. Health and metric scrapes are exempt.
The limiter is global to one process, not per user/IP; it does not trust forwarded
IP headers. Use gateway authentication and per-client limits for shared deployments.

## Metrics and diagnostic events

```sh
mcp-gmap-rs --log-format json serve http --metrics --rate-limit 120
```

`GET /metrics` uses the same bearer token as `/mcp` when configured. On an
unauthenticated loopback listener it is also unauthenticated. It is disabled by
default, and native mTLS applies when enabled. Expose it only to trusted scrapers.
The Prometheus text endpoint exports:

- `mcp_gmap_tool_calls_total{tool,outcome}` for completed tool calls;
- `mcp_gmap_tool_duration_seconds{tool,outcome}` as a histogram;
- `mcp_gmap_google_requests_total{api,status}` for Google HTTP attempts, including retries;
- `mcp_gmap_http_rate_limited_total` for rejected HTTP requests.

Labels contain built-in tool names, API hostnames, HTTP status codes and fixed
outcomes. They never contain addresses, coordinates, credentials, tokens or session
IDs. A composite with per-item errors may count as a successful top-level call;
inspect its result and the upstream status metrics. Metrics reset on restart.

Set `RUST_LOG=info` to see tool completion events with name, success and elapsed
time. Arguments and Google response bodies are not included. The listener's startup
address is printed separately on stderr. Stdout remains CLI JSON or MCP traffic.

## Doctor

```sh
mcp-gmap-rs doctor
# Explicit opt-in: makes potentially billable requests.
mcp-gmap-rs doctor --live
# Check only the API dependencies of selected tools:
mcp-gmap-rs --enabled-tools maps_pollen,maps_area_insights doctor --live
```

Without `--live`, doctor checks local credential configuration, HTTP settings and
TLS file/key matching without making network requests. It does not prove key
validity, IAM, API enablement, certificate trust/hostname/expiry or ADC access.
ADC discovery is reported as `not_tested` until a live request. Doctor never
prints credential values or their JSON. A JSON report goes to stdout; a failed
check produces exit status 1. Parse `checks[].status`: `pass`, `fail` or `not_tested`.

Live mode makes one representative tool invocation for each distinct Google API
used by enabled tools, with normal retry/deadline/budget settings. It avoids running
expensive composites. Routes use exact coordinates. Roads uses nearest-road lookup.
Probes use public Paris landmarks, not user-provided addresses. Success means Google
accepted that probe, not that every operation or geographic region is available.


## Shutdown and configuration changes

Ctrl-C and SIGTERM shut down the HTTP server and its active MCP sessions. The
Kubernetes example gives the process 30 seconds. Other application configuration,
including environment-injected Secret changes, requires a restart; only native TLS
certificate/key/client-CA files support SIGHUP reload. Sessions and metrics are
in memory and are lost on restart. Run a single replica or configure session
affinity; clients must reconnect when their owning process exits.

See [Deployment](./deployment) for container permissions, probes and runtime
credential mounts, and [Configuration reference](../reference/configuration) for
every setting and flag.


<!-- https://fcenedes.github.io/mcp-gmap-rs/guide/recipes -->

# Recipes

Combine small, explicit calls around one location or a shortlist of returned place IDs. These examples make potentially billable Google requests. Review [authentication](./authentication) first; composites may use more than one API and return partial errors.

## Find a cafe and compare the trip

Search within a real radius, expand only shortlisted IDs, then compare travel. Nearby’s `keyword` is a Google place type, not free text.

```sh
mcp-gmap-rs search-nearby \
  --center '{"value":"48.8584,2.2945","isCoordinates":true}' \
  --keyword cafe --radius 500 --open-now --min-rating 4
mcp-gmap-rs place-details --place-id ChIJLU7jZClu5kcR4PcOOO6p3I0 --max-photos 0
mcp-gmap-rs distance-matrix --origins '["48.8584,2.2945"]' \
  --destinations '["48.8606,2.3376","48.8530,2.3499"]' --mode walking
```

Use [`search-places`](../reference/tools#maps_search_places) for natural-language intent, [`compare-places`](../reference/tools#maps_compare_places) for detailed matches with optional driving distance, or [`explore-area`](../reference/tools#maps_explore_area) for category-based exploration. A search page is not an exhaustive inventory. Preserve Google source links, review authors and AI disclosures.

## Plan stops and find a detour

```sh
mcp-gmap-rs plan-route \
  --stops '["48.8584,2.2945","48.8606,2.3376","48.8530,2.3499"]' \
  --mode walking --optimize false
mcp-gmap-rs search-along-route --text-query cafes \
  --origin '48.8584,2.2945' --destination '48.8606,2.3376' \
  --mode walking --max-results 3
```

[`directions`](../reference/tools#maps_directions) handles one journey with time/avoidance options; [`plan-route`](../reference/tools#maps_plan_route) preserves endpoints when optimizing intermediates. Transit accepts only two total stops. Along-route search follows a polyline instead of substituting a midpoint circle. It defaults to walking, so always choose the intended travel mode.

## Resolve once, inspect local conditions

```sh
mcp-gmap-rs geocode --address 'Eiffel Tower, Paris, France'
mcp-gmap-rs weather --latitude 48.8584 --longitude 2.2945 \
  --type forecast_daily --forecast-days 3
mcp-gmap-rs air-quality --latitude 48.8584 --longitude 2.2945
mcp-gmap-rs pollen --latitude 48.8584 --longitude 2.2945 --days 3
mcp-gmap-rs timezone --latitude 48.8584 --longitude 2.2945
mcp-gmap-rs elevation --locations '[{"latitude":48.8584,"longitude":2.2945}]'
```

Reuse coordinates instead of repeating resolution. Keep observations, forecasts and provider recommendations distinct; coverage can vary. [`reverse-geocode`](../reference/tools#maps_reverse_geocode) resolves coordinates back to an address; [`batch-geocode`](../reference/tools#maps_batch_geocode) resolves up to 50 addresses with per-address errors. Time Zone’s optional timestamp uses Unix milliseconds; elevation is in metres.

## Validate a postal address

```sh
mcp-gmap-rs validate-address --address-lines '["5 Avenue Anatole France"]' \
  --locality Paris --postal-code 75007 --region-code FR
```

Inspect the verdict, corrections and unresolved components. Address validation is distinct from geocoding and does not guarantee delivery. USPS CASS is opt-in and requires `regionCode` US or PR in this implementation.

## Count places without counting search hits

```sh
mcp-gmap-rs area-insights \
  --area '{"circle":{"latLng":{"latitude":48.8584,"longitude":2.2945},"radius":500}}' \
  --included-types '["restaurant"]' --min-rating 4
```

Aggregate counts normally use Google’s string int64 representation. Optional place IDs are available only when the count is at most 100; details are not fetched automatically. For explicitly requested visibility analysis, [`local-rank-tracker`](../reference/tools#maps_local_rank_tracker) measures keyword ranks across a grid. Start with one keyword and a 3×3 grid; ranks are not review ratings, and failed points must stay visible.

## Match GPS data and save a map

Use [`snap-to-roads`](../reference/tools#maps_snap_to_roads) for an ordered trace and [`nearest-roads`](../reference/tools#maps_nearest_roads) for independent points. Preserve `originalIndex`; interpolation adds points that may not have one. Speed limits are not returned.

```sh
mcp-gmap-rs nearest-roads --points '[{"latitude":48.8584,"longitude":2.2945}]'
mcp-gmap-rs static-map --center '48.8584,2.2945' --zoom 14 --output area.png
```

The [tool reference](../reference/tools) lists exact bounds, required fields, defaults and result formats for every operation.


<!-- https://fcenedes.github.io/mcp-gmap-rs/guide/troubleshooting -->

# Troubleshooting

First identify the failing connection: a local configuration error, the MCP client-to-server connection, or an outbound Google request. Correct the relevant layer, then rerun the affected operation.

## Start offline

```sh
mcp-gmap-rs --version
mcp-gmap-rs tools
mcp-gmap-rs doctor
```

`doctor` prints JSON even when checks fail. Inspect its exit status and `checks[].status`: `pass`, `fail` or `not_tested`. Offline checks do not prove IAM, API enablement, billing, certificate trust/expiry or ADC access. `/health` only proves process liveness.

If a malformed local dotenv file blocks discovery, `--no-env-file tools` skips it. This can change the selected tool set, so do not mistake it for verification of the intended file configuration.

## Interpret common failures

| Symptom | Next check |
| --- | --- |
| `GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY is required` | API-key mode is selected or this operation reaches a key-only endpoint. |
| `GOOGLE_CLOUD_QUOTA_PROJECT is required` | Set the consumer project ID/number for OAuth. |
| Google 403 / API disabled | Enable the exact API in the credential’s consumer project; check billing and API-key restrictions. |
| `serviceusage.services.use` denied | Grant the service account `roles/serviceusage.serviceUsageConsumer` on the quota project; allow IAM propagation, then retry. |
| API-key IP denial | Allow the server or cluster’s public egress IP, not its private pod IP. |
| MCP HTTP 401 | Send the server’s bearer token; a Google access token authenticates a different connection. |
| Host/Origin rejected | Match the configured Host and browser origin exactly, including relevant ports. |
| HTTP 429 from MCP | The process-wide limiter is exhausted; honor `Retry-After` and check client concurrency. |
| OAuth timeout | Check token/STS/IAM or metadata connectivity, system clock and per-request timeout. |
| TLS connection fails | Check the certificate chain, hostname, trust and optional mTLS client certificate separately from HTTP authorization. |
| Exit 0 but incomplete data | Inspect matrix/composite per-item errors, not just the process exit status. |

## Verify live access deliberately

Live probes make potentially billable calls. Scope them to the API dependencies you need:

```sh
mcp-gmap-rs --enabled-tools maps_weather doctor --live
```

A passing probe does not guarantee every geographic region or operation. After a Google Cloud change, rerun the same failed call rather than inferring success from console settings. See [authentication](./authentication) for IAM and credential sources, [configuration](./configuration) for precedence and [production operations](./production) for budgets, deadlines and metrics. Never print credential JSON or dump the environment into an issue report.


<!-- https://fcenedes.github.io/mcp-gmap-rs/reference/configuration -->

# Configuration reference

These 21 application settings apply to CLI, MCP stdio and Streamable HTTP as appropriate. Values follow **defaults → optional dotenv → environment → flags**. See [configuration](../guide/configuration) for file selection and override semantics.

Global flags go before a tool or `serve`; HTTP-only flags go after `serve http`. A dash in the flag column means there is no corresponding CLI flag: inject that value through the environment or selected dotenv file.

## Google access and tool execution

| Environment variable | Default | CLI flag | Meaning and accepted values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY` | Unset | — | Restricted Google API key. Required in `api-key` mode and for this implementation’s key-only endpoints, including when OAuth mode is selected. Never a tool argument. |
| `GOOGLE_MAPS_AUTH_MODE` | `api-key` | `--auth-mode` | `api-key` or `oauth`. OAuth supports Places (New), Routes, Weather, Air Quality, Address Validation and Places Aggregate. |
| `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` | ADC discovery | — | Readable service-account or supported ADC JSON file path. Relative paths use the working directory. Leave unset for local ADC or metadata discovery. |
| `GOOGLE_CLOUD_QUOTA_PROJECT` | Unset | — | Required consumer billing/quota project ID or number for OAuth calls. The service account needs `serviceusage.services.use` in that project. |
| `GOOGLE_MAPS_LANGUAGE` | `en` | `--language` | Language code for language-aware Google responses. Independent of this manual’s language selector. |
| `GOOGLE_MAPS_TIMEOUT` | `30` | `--timeout` | Per-request timeout in seconds, integer 1–600. Includes queueing, retries, backoff and response reads; OAuth acquisition has its own bound using the same value. |
| `GOOGLE_MAPS_ENABLED_TOOLS` | All (`*`) | `--enabled-tools` | Comma-separated `maps_*` names or `*`. Unknown names fail startup. Disabled tools are absent from discovery and cannot be called. |
| `GOOGLE_MAPS_MAX_REQUESTS` | `200` | `--max-requests` | Google HTTP attempt budget per tool invocation, integer 1–10000. Shared across composite branches; retries consume attempts. |
| `GOOGLE_MAPS_MAX_RETRIES` | `2` | `--max-retries` | Additional transient attempts per Google request, integer 0–5. Zero means one initial attempt. Retries remain within timeout and budget. |
| `GOOGLE_MAPS_TOOL_TIMEOUT` | `120` | `--tool-timeout` | Overall tool deadline in seconds, integer 1–3600. Includes credential acquisition, queueing, API calls and retries. |

Five Google HTTP requests can execute concurrently per process. The attempt budget limits requests rather than currency; one matrix request can bill multiple elements. Some composites return per-item errors when a branch exhausts its budget or deadline. See [production limits](../guide/production#limits-retries-and-deadlines).

## HTTP listener and access

| Environment variable | Default | HTTP flag | Meaning and accepted values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `MCP_HTTP_TOKEN` | Unset | — | Shared bearer token for MCP clients. Required for non-loopback binds. Separate from Google credentials and still required with native mTLS. |
| `MCP_HTTP_LISTEN` | `127.0.0.1:3000` | `--listen` | Listener IP address and port. The Docker image sets the environment value to `0.0.0.0:3000`. |
| `MCP_HTTP_ALLOWED_HOSTS` | Loopback hosts | `--allowed-host` | Comma-separated accepted HTTP Host values. Repeat the flag for several values; flags replace the whole file/environment list. Include the relevant port. |
| `MCP_HTTP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` | None | `--allowed-origin` | Comma-separated allowed browser origins. Present Origin headers are rejected unless allowed. Specify ports explicitly; repeated flags replace the list. |
| `MCP_HTTP_RATE_LIMIT` | `120` | `--rate-limit` | Authenticated `/mcp` requests per minute per process, integer 0–1000000. Zero disables. Burst capacity equals the rate; continuous refill. |
| `MCP_METRICS_ENABLED` | `false` | `--metrics [true\|false]` | Enable Prometheus `/metrics`. A bare `--metrics` means true. Uses the same bearer credential when configured; native mTLS also applies. |
| `MCP_TLS_CERT` | Unset | `--tls-cert` | PEM server leaf certificate plus intermediate chain. Must be supplied together with a matching private key. |
| `MCP_TLS_KEY` | Unset | `--tls-key` | PEM server private key path. Keep readable by the runtime identity and out of source/images. |
| `MCP_TLS_CLIENT_CA` | Unset | `--tls-client-ca` | PEM client CA bundle enabling mandatory client certificates on every listener path. Does not replace the bearer token. |

The HTTP token bucket is global to the process, not per user/IP. Unauthorized requests do not consume it; health and metrics are exempt. Rejections return 429 with `Retry-After`. The request-body limit is 1 MiB. See [MCP access](../guide/mcp#bind-addresses-and-access) and [TLS operations](../guide/production#native-tls-and-mutual-tls).

## Diagnostic events

| Environment variable | Default | CLI flag | Meaning and accepted values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `RUST_LOG` | `warn` | — | Diagnostic log filter. `info` enables tool completion events; arguments and Google response bodies are not logged. |
| `MCP_LOG_FORMAT` | `text` | `--log-format` | `text` or `json`. Diagnostics always go to stderr, leaving stdout for CLI JSON or MCP traffic. |

## File selection and output controls

File selection happens before the application layers above. `MCP_ENV_FILE` chooses a dotenv path; global `--env-file PATH` takes precedence. An explicitly selected file must exist. `--no-env-file` disables all dotenv loading and conflicts with `--env-file`. Without a selection, only the working directory’s optional `.env` is read.

An explicitly empty environment value still overrides a file value. It can clear an optional token, TLS path or allowlist; it does not make an empty numeric setting valid. Loaded file values do not mutate the process environment.

`doctor --live` opts into potentially billable probes; ordinary `doctor` is offline. Tool `--output PATH` saves JSON, or raw PNG for `static-map`. These are command controls, not additional environment settings.

Application settings and credential-file changes require a restart. On Linux/macOS, SIGHUP can reload native TLS certificate/key/client-CA files together; failed reloads preserve the previous TLS configuration. See [configuration](../guide/configuration) and [production operations](../guide/production).

# Tool reference

All 23 tools, with every parameter, default, constraint and example. The same interface is available through MCP and the CLI.

## Calling conventions

The examples are MCP argument objects. For a raw MCP `tools/call`, use the tool name as `name` and the object as `arguments`. Hosts may prefix tool names. The equivalent CLI calls below use `mcp-gmap-rs call TOOL --args JSON`.

Only top-level parameters have CLI flags. Pass nested objects and arrays as JSON. A bare boolean flag means `true`; `--flag false` sets `false`. Unknown properties are rejected. Inspect your installed release with `tools` or `schema TOOL`.

Google authentication and language are process configuration, not tool parameters. Exact route coordinates avoid address resolution; named locations may also require an API key for Geocoding. See [authentication](../guide/authentication) and [configuration](../guide/configuration).

Calls can incur Google charges. Composite and matrix results may contain per-item errors even when the tool succeeds. Preserve Google source links, review/photo authors and AI-summary disclosures. Examples illustrate inputs, not current coverage or results.

Types, required fields and schema bounds come from the executable's schema-derived reference. Defaults, result descriptions and cross-field restrictions are reviewed against the implementation. Google may impose additional coverage and quota limits.

- [`maps_area_insights`](#maps_area_insights)

## maps_geocode {#maps_geocode}

Convert an address or landmark to coordinates.

Resolve an address or landmark to the first Geocoding match. Use this to obtain reusable coordinates and a place ID; it does not validate postal deliverability.

**CLI command:** `geocode`. **Google access:** API key required in this implementation.

### Parameters

| Parameter / CLI flag | Type and schema limits | Required | Default when omitted | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `address` / `--address` | string; at least 1 character(s) | Yes | — | Address, city or landmark to geocode. |

### Behavior and restrictions

- No match is a tool error, not an empty successful location.
- This direct tool uses Geocoding v3; Places fallback is used by location-resolving composites, not by this call.

### Result

An object with `location.lat`, `location.lng`, `formatted_address` and `place_id`. Only the first result is returned.

### Example

MCP arguments:

```json
{
  "address": "Eiffel Tower, Paris, France"
}
```

Equivalent CLI call:

```sh
mcp-gmap-rs call maps_geocode --args '{"address":"Eiffel Tower, Paris, France"}'
```


## maps_validate_address {#maps_validate_address}

Validate and standardize a postal address; returns Google's verdict, corrections, components and geocode. A verdict is evidence, not a delivery guarantee.

Validate postal components and return corrections, the standardized address and Google’s verdict. Keep the verdict and unresolved components visible to the caller.

**CLI command:** `validate-address`. **Google access:** API key or OAuth for the main API.

### Parameters

| Parameter / CLI flag | Type and schema limits | Required | Default when omitted | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `addressLines` / `--address-lines` | array of string; 1–10 items; each item at least 1 character(s) | Yes | — | One or more postal-address lines, in order. |
| `administrativeArea` / `--administrative-area` | string; at least 1 character(s) | No | Not supplied | State, province or corresponding administrative area. |
| `enableUspsCass` / `--enable-usps-cass` | boolean | No | false | Request USPS CASS processing; this implementation requires regionCode US or PR when true. |
| `locality` / `--locality` | string; at least 1 character(s) | No | Not supplied | City or locality. |
| `postalCode` / `--postal-code` | string; at least 1 character(s) | No | Not supplied | Postal/ZIP code. |
| `regionCode` / `--region-code` | string; pattern: `^[A-Z]{2}$` | No | Not supplied; Google may infer it | Two-letter uppercase country/region code; recommended to disambiguate the address. |

### Behavior and restrictions

- A validation verdict is not a delivery guarantee.
- Region/API coverage varies. This tool does not submit validation feedback or automatically accept corrections.

### Result

The complete validation response, typically including `result.verdict`, `result.address`, `result.geocode` and `responseId`; Google may omit unavailable fields.

### Example

MCP arguments:

```json
{
  "addressLines": [
    "5 Avenue Anatole France"
  ],
  "regionCode": "FR",
  "locality": "Paris",
  "postalCode": "75007"
}
```

Equivalent CLI call:

```sh
mcp-gmap-rs call maps_validate_address --args '{"addressLines":["5 Avenue Anatole France"],"regionCode":"FR","locality":"Paris","postalCode":"75007"}'
```


## maps_pollen {#maps_pollen}

Get 1-5 days of pollen forecasts, indices and health recommendations for exact coordinates. Coverage varies by location and season.

Retrieve a short daily pollen forecast for exact coordinates. The response preserves pollen types, indices, plant information and provider recommendations.

**CLI command:** `pollen`. **Google access:** API key required in this implementation.

### Parameters

| Parameter / CLI flag | Type and schema limits | Required | Default when omitted | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `days` / `--days` | integer; 1–5 | No | 1 | Number of daily forecast records to request. |
| `latitude` / `--latitude` | number; -90.0–90.0 | Yes | — | WGS84 latitude in decimal degrees; north is positive. |
| `longitude` / `--longitude` | number; -180.0–180.0 | Yes | — | WGS84 longitude in decimal degrees; east is positive. |
| `plantsDescription` / `--plants-description` | boolean | No | false | Include detailed plant descriptions and related information when available. |

### Behavior and restrictions

- Requests use a page size of 5, sufficient for this tool’s maximum five-day request; no additional pages are fetched automatically.
- Availability depends on location, season and Google coverage.

### Result

The original Pollen response, including `regionCode`, `dailyInfo` and any `nextPageToken`. Each day can include pollen-type and plant information.

### Example

MCP arguments:

```json
{
  "latitude": 48.8584,
  "longitude": 2.2945,
  "days": 3,
  "plantsDescription": false
}
```

Equivalent CLI call:

```sh
mcp-gmap-rs call maps_pollen --args '{"latitude":48.8584,"longitude":2.2945,"days":3,"plantsDescription":false}'
```


## maps_area_insights {#maps_area_insights}

Count places within a circle, region or polygon using Places Aggregate. Optional place IDs are available only for counts of 100 or less; no automatic details requests.

Count matching places in a circle, region or polygon with Places Aggregate. This is an aggregate query rather than a count of a limited Places search page.

**CLI command:** `area-insights`. **Google access:** API key or OAuth for the main API.

### Parameters

| Parameter / CLI flag | Type and schema limits | Required | Default when omitted | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `area` / `--area` | object | Yes | — | Exactly one of circle, region or customArea. |
| `area.circle` | object | No | Not supplied | Circular area; mutually exclusive with region/customArea. |
| `area.circle.latLng` | object | When parent is supplied | — | Circle center as exact coordinates. |
| `area.circle.latLng.latitude` | number; -90.0–90.0 | When parent is supplied | — | WGS84 latitude in decimal degrees; north is positive. |
| `area.circle.latLng.longitude` | number; -180.0–180.0 | When parent is supplied | — | WGS84 longitude in decimal degrees; east is positive. |
| `area.circle.radius` | integer; 23–50000 | When parent is supplied | — | Circle radius in metres. |
| `area.customArea` | object | No | Not supplied | Custom polygon area; mutually exclusive with circle/region. |
| `area.customArea.polygon` | object | When parent is supplied | — | Polygon boundary. |
| `area.customArea.polygon.coordinates` | array of object; 4–1000 items | When parent is supplied | — | Ordered ring of coordinate objects; first and last coordinates must match. |
| `area.customArea.polygon.coordinates[].latitude` | number; -90.0–90.0 | When parent is supplied | — | WGS84 latitude in decimal degrees; north is positive. |
| `area.customArea.polygon.coordinates[].longitude` | number; -180.0–180.0 | When parent is supplied | — | WGS84 longitude in decimal degrees; east is positive. |
| `area.region` | object | No | Not supplied | An administrative/geographic region identified by a Google place resource. |
| `area.region.place` | string; pattern: `^places/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$` | When parent is supplied | — | Region resource in places/PLACE_ID format, not a free-form region name. |
| `excludedTypes` / `--excluded-types` | array of string; 1–50 items; each item at least 1 character(s) | No | No excluded-type filter | Google place types to exclude. |
| `includePlaces` / `--include-places` | boolean | No | false | Request matching place resource IDs in addition to the count. |
| `includedTypes` / `--included-types` | array of string; 1–50 items; each item at least 1 character(s) | Yes | — | Google place types to include, such as restaurant or cafe. |
| `maxRating` / `--max-rating` | number; 1.0–5.0 | No | No upper rating filter | Inclusive upper rating bound. |
| `minRating` / `--min-rating` | number; 1.0–5.0 | No | No lower rating filter | Inclusive lower rating bound; cannot exceed maxRating. |
| `operatingStatus` / `--operating-status` | array of string; 1–3 items; values: `OPERATING_STATUS_OPERATIONAL`, `OPERATING_STATUS_PERMANENTLY_CLOSED`, `OPERATING_STATUS_TEMPORARILY_CLOSED` | No | Google defaults to operational places | Allowed operating states. |
| `priceLevels` / `--price-levels` | array of string; 1–5 items; values: `PRICE_LEVEL_FREE`, `PRICE_LEVEL_INEXPENSIVE`, `PRICE_LEVEL_MODERATE`, `PRICE_LEVEL_EXPENSIVE`, `PRICE_LEVEL_VERY_EXPENSIVE` | No | All price levels | Allowed price levels. |

### Behavior and restrictions

- Supply exactly one area form. Nested objects are JSON values on the CLI; their child parameters do not have independent flags.
- Polygon rings must be closed. Google also checks polygon geometry, supported types, area and coverage.
- Place IDs are available only for counts of 100 or less. The tool does not automatically request Place Details.

### Result

Google’s response with `count` (normally an int64 string) and optional `placeInsights[].place` resources when IDs were requested and available.

### Example

MCP arguments:

```json
{
  "area": {
    "circle": {
      "latLng": {
        "latitude": 48.8584,
        "longitude": 2.2945
      },
      "radius": 500
    }
  },
  "includedTypes": [
    "restaurant"
  ],
  "minRating": 4
}
```

Equivalent CLI call:

```sh
mcp-gmap-rs call maps_area_insights --args '{"area":{"circle":{"latLng":{"latitude":48.8584,"longitude":2.2945},"radius":500}},"includedTypes":["restaurant"],"minRating":4}'
```


## maps_snap_to_roads {#maps_snap_to_roads}

Snap an ordered GPS path of 2-100 points to roads. Keep consecutive points within about 300 metres for good results. Optional interpolation adds road geometry.

Match an ordered GPS trace to the most likely road geometry. Use Nearest Roads for independent points rather than a travelled path.

**CLI command:** `snap-to-roads`. **Google access:** API key required in this implementation.

### Parameters

| Parameter / CLI flag | Type and schema limits | Required | Default when omitted | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `interpolate` / `--interpolate` | boolean | No | false | Add intermediate road geometry between supplied points. |
| `path` / `--path` | array of object; 2–100 items | Yes | — | GPS coordinate objects in travel order. |
| `path[].latitude` | number; -90.0–90.0 | When parent is supplied | — | WGS84 latitude in decimal degrees; north is positive. |
| `path[].longitude` | number; -180.0–180.0 | When parent is supplied | — | WGS84 longitude in decimal degrees; east is positive. |

### Behavior and restrictions

- Consecutive input points should be within about 300 metres for good matching.
- Interpolated points may not have an originalIndex. Speed limits are not requested by this tool.

### Result

The original Roads response, including `snappedPoints` and any `warningMessage`. Points preserve road `placeId`, `location` and `originalIndex` when provided.

### Example

MCP arguments:

```json
{
  "path": [
    {
      "latitude": -35.27801,
      "longitude": 149.12958
    },
    {
      "latitude": -35.28032,
      "longitude": 149.12907
    }
  ],
  "interpolate": true
}
```

Equivalent CLI call:

```sh
mcp-gmap-rs call maps_snap_to_roads --args '{"path":[{"latitude":-35.27801,"longitude":149.12958},{"latitude":-35.28032,"longitude":149.12907}],"interpolate":true}'
```


## maps_nearest_roads {#maps_nearest_roads}

Find the nearest road segments for 1-100 independent GPS points; preserves Google's originalIndex and road place IDs.

Find nearby road segments for independent GPS points without interpreting them as one continuous trace.

**CLI command:** `nearest-roads`. **Google access:** API key required in this implementation.

### Parameters

| Parameter / CLI flag | Type and schema limits | Required | Default when omitted | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `points` / `--points` | array of object; 1–100 items | Yes | — | Independent coordinate objects to match. |
| `points[].latitude` | number; -90.0–90.0 | When parent is supplied | — | WGS84 latitude in decimal degrees; north is positive. |
| `points[].longitude` | number; -180.0–180.0 | When parent is supplied | — | WGS84 longitude in decimal degrees; east is positive. |

### Behavior and restrictions

- A point can match more than one road segment; retain originalIndex rather than assuming one output per input.
- Speed limits are not requested by this tool.

### Result

The original Roads response with `snappedPoints`, road `placeId`, `location` and `originalIndex` mapping back to input points.

### Example

MCP arguments:

```json
{
  "points": [
    {
      "latitude": -35.27801,
      "longitude": 149.12958
    },
    {
      "latitude": -35.28032,
      "longitude": 149.12907
    }
  ]
}
```

Equivalent CLI call:

```sh
mcp-gmap-rs call maps_nearest_roads --args '{"points":[{"latitude":-35.27801,"longitude":149.12958},{"latitude":-35.28032,"longitude":149.12907}]}'
```


## maps_reverse_geocode {#maps_reverse_geocode}

Convert coordinates to a street address.

Convert exact coordinates to the first reverse-Geocoding result. Use the result’s components when a formatted address alone is insufficient.

**CLI command:** `reverse-geocode`. **Google access:** API key required in this implementation.

| Parameter / CLI flag | Type and schema limits | Required | Default when omitted | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `longitude` / `--longitude` | number; -180.0–180.0 | Yes | — | WGS84 longitude in decimal degrees; east is positive. |

### Behavior and restrictions

- Only the first result is returned. No match is a tool error.

The first native Geocoding result, including `formatted_address`, `address_components`, `geometry` and `place_id` when available.
